Audience: first-time Hawaii class three applicants, including minors on the graduated path, learning icy danger spots, dawn and dusk glare, night driving precautions, freeway planning, entering, driving, emergency stops and exiting, and the emergency procedures for blowouts, lost wheels, brake and steering failure, wheels off the pavement, passing conflicts, oncoming vehicles, a stuck accelerator, skids, fire and breakdowns in plain English.

Prerequisites: the braking, passing and lane-change techniques of the two previous sections, which the freeway and emergency procedures assume.

Scope note: winter danger spots, dawn and dusk glare, night driving precautions and high-beam etiquette, freeway trip planning, entering, driving, emergency stops and exiting, the basic emergency principles, and the procedures for blowouts, lost wheels, brake and steering failure, wheels off the pavement, passing conflicts, oncoming vehicles, a stuck accelerator, power steering failure, skids, fire and breakdowns. Sharing the road with large vehicles and motorcycles follows in the next section.

Recall emphasis: the ordered steps of each procedure are practiced as recall items, while choosing the right response to a described emergency feeds the dedicated scene-decision surface declared in part C.
